name: Iraqi maqam of Baghdad
lineage: Iraqi maqam ("al-maqam al-iraqi") classical modal-suite tradition of Baghdad and the broader Iraqi cultural area, with development through the Ottoman-Mamluk and Ottoman-Hashemite periods into the twentieth-century canonical form. The Iraqi maqam repertoire comprises approximately fifty-six canonical maqamat ("modal-suites"), each organized as a multi-movement suite including tahrir (opening melismatic-improvisation movement), miyana (middle-register heightened-emotional section), and taslim (concluding-return cadential section). Performance configuration centers on the male qari (singer-reciter, a respected community-cultural-figure trained through extended apprenticeship) accompanied by the chalghi instrumental ensemble: joza (four-string spike-fiddle with coconut-shell resonator, the lead instrument), santur (struck-board-zither, distantly cognate with the Persian santur and the European hammered dulcimer), riqq (small tambourine with brass jingles), dumbek (goblet-drum), and naqqarat (small kettle-drum pair). Lyric base draws on classical Arabic poetry, with particularly heavy use of the seventh-century pre-Islamic mu'allaqat poetic tradition and the medieval Arabic poets al-Mutanabbi and Abu Nuwas. Modal vocabulary draws on the Arabic maqam framework with characteristic Iraqi-specific maqamat (such as maqam Bayat al-Iraqi, maqam Awj al-Iraqi) that have no exact parallel in Egyptian or Levantine maqam practice. Twentieth-century canonical qari include Mohammed al-Qubanchi (1900-1989), Yousuf Omar (1918-1987), and Hashim al-Rajab. Scheherezade Hassan's scholarship constitutes the principal Western-distributed academic documentation. Distinguished from Egyptian and Levantine maqam by Iraqi's joza-and-santur (vs oud-and-qanun) instrumental ensemble base; distinguished from Iranian dastgah and Azerbaijani mugham by Arabic-language repertoire and Baghdadi-specific maqamat; distinguished from Yemeni Sanaani by Iraqi maqam's suite-of-movements (vs Yemeni qomah-with-three-movements) architecture.
